entry.title: A researcher's journey to Virginia Tech

media:group.media:title: A researcher's journey to Virginia Tech
media:group.media:description: Petr Maca, a postdoctoral researcher working with Eric Jacques, came to Virginia Tech through the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Postdoctoral Fellowship. Using the university’s unique Shock Tube facility, Maca studies explosions and materials testing at a level that drew him halfway across the world. As he puts it, Virginia Tech was “the only place in the world where I could do work like this.”

entry.title: What happens when students try miracle fruit?

media:group.media:title: What happens when students try miracle fruit?
media:group.media:description:
Students at Virginia Tech recently put the "miracle fruit" to the test inside the Biological Sciences Plant Teaching Collection. This unique berry contains a compound called miraculin, which temporarily changes how our taste receptors respond to acidic foods, creating a surprising tasting experience.
Beyond the fun experiment, the experience gave students a firsthand look at the power of scientific curiosity and discovery. With more than 200 plant species, the Biological Sciences Plant Teaching Collection provides opportunities for students to engage directly with living specimens, explore plant diversity, and connect classroom learning to real-world observation.
At Virginia Tech, memorable learning experiences often begin with a simple question: "What happens if we try this?" Sometimes the answer is sweeter than expected.

media:group.media:title: Virginia Tech research reaches orbit
media:group.media:description:
Virginia Tech researchers send a research experiment to the International Space Station to study how wounds heal in microgravity. Working alongside collaborators from the University of Virginia and Space Tango, the team develop specialized sensors that monitor the mechanical properties of 3D cell culture models over time.
The project combines advanced engineering, biomedical research, and commercial spaceflight technology to investigate how the body's healing processes may differ in microgravity. After years of development, testing, and sensor selection, the experiment is launched to the International Space Station, marking a major milestone for the researchers, students, and partners involved.

media:group.media:title: Engineers reimagine 3D metal printing
media:group.media:description: Virginia Tech researchers are exploring robotic additive friction stir deposition (AFSD), an advanced manufacturing process that enables the production of metal components without fully melting the material. It's similar to 3D printing. The technology's flexibility and multi-axis capabilities could benefit industries ranging from aerospace and defense to energy and shipbuilding.

entry.title: What LEGO wind turbines can teach students about data science

media:group.media:title: What LEGO wind turbines can teach students about data science
media:group.media:description:
What does it really take to become a data scientist? In Virginia Tech's Master of Science in Data Science (MSDS) program, students learn that successful data science is about much more than building predictive models.
In this hands-on classroom experience, students design and build miniature wind turbines using LEGO components, collect real-world performance data, and analyze the differences between healthy and defective turbine blades. Through the project, they gain practical experience across the entire data science lifecycle, from problem discovery and data collection to data preparation, modeling, deployment, and monitoring.

entry.title: Building tomorrow’s workforce in the heart of D.C.

media:group.media:title: Building tomorrow’s workforce in the heart of D.C.
media:group.media:description:
Virginia Tech’s growing innovation network in the greater Washington, D.C., area prepares students for the workforce of tomorrow and brings together leading researchers, industry partners, and national policymakers to address some of the world’s most urgent challenges. In this vibrant hub, faculty and students work with industry to advance research and innovation in artificial intelligence, wireless technology, quantum computing, national security and other emerging fields. Through project-based learning and partnerships, students gain experience solving real-world problems while faculty research drives meaningful impact.
Guided by our land-grant mission, Ut Prosim (That I May Serve), Virginia Tech brings together talent, ideas, and partnerships to create lasting impact.

entry.title: Assistant Secretary of Energy visits Virginia Tech to see the future of mining

media:group.media:title: Assistant Secretary of Energy visits Virginia Tech to see the future of mining
media:group.media:description: During a visit to Virginia Tech, Assistant Secretary of Energy for the U.S. Department of Energy Audrey Robertson, highlighted the growing need for mining engineers. The visit showcased how Virginia Tech is preparing the next generation of engineers through interdisciplinary education that combines mining, robotics, artificial intelligence, autonomy, and wireless communications.

entry.title: Virginia Peanuts: Growing the Best from the Ground Up

media:group.media:title: Virginia Peanuts: Growing the Best from the Ground Up
media:group.media:description:
Virginia peanuts are famous for being large, gourmet-style peanuts that are often sold and roasted in the shell. They play a vital role in the region’s agricultural economy, generating millions of dollars annually and supporting local businesses, jobs, and farming communities.
Researchers at Virginia Tech's Tidewater Agricultural Research and Extension Center, Extension specialists, and producers work together to improve peanut production through field trials, variety evaluations, disease-resistance testing, harvest-timing recommendations, and quality assessments. Their research helps growers adopt the best management practices, increase yields, and produce high-quality peanuts, while continuing Virginia’s long-standing legacy as a leader in peanut production and innovation.
